subject: rating-scale
detail: Shelfie's README and openapi.yaml say ratings are 1-10 in a field named 'score'; Shelfie's code (handler and DB CHECK) and Readr's code both use 1-5 in a field named 'stars'. Building from the docs would make every existing rating mean something different.
solutions: Follow the code: 1-5 integer 'stars' (both apps agree)
Follow Shelfie's docs: 1-10 'score' and rescale any imported data
recommended: Follow the code: integer 'stars' 1-5, enforced in the API and by a DB CHECK; correct the docs in the new app

subject: export-format
detail: Shelfie's README and spec promise CSV at GET /api/v1/books/export.csv; the code serves JSON at GET /api/books/export. The CSV export was never built.
solutions: Build JSON export as the code does
Build CSV as the docs say
recommended: JSON export as the code does (user: trust what the apps do); CSV recorded as an open question, not built

subject: path-prefix
detail: Spec uses /api/v1/...; code uses /api/... with no version. Neither app has clients we know of.
solutions: New app uses /api/v1 for every endpoint
recommended: New app uses /api/v1 for every endpoint (one versioning scheme); there is no observed client of the old paths to keep compatible

subject: documented-services-and-database
detail: Shelfie's docs describe three services (catalog, ratings, gateway) each with its own database, on PostgreSQL; the code is one process with one SQLite file and no gateway.
solutions: Design from the code: one process, one database
Design from the docs: three services with a gateway
recommended: Ignore the stale service and PostgreSQL claims; choose the architecture on this project's drivers in phase 5

subject: undocumented-session-secret
detail: Shelfie requires SHELFIE_SESSION_SECRET at startup but never uses it, and no doc mentions it.
solutions: Give the new app a documented session secret it actually uses
recommended: One documented SESSION_SECRET in the config module and .env.example (name only), used to sign session cookies

subject: rating-cardinality-and-durability
detail: Both apps append a new ratings row on every rating (no key, no uniqueness) and neither ever commits, so ratings pile up and are lost on exit; Shelfie's export repeats a book once per rating.
solutions: One rating per user per book, upsert, commit every write
recommended: Rating has a unique (user_id, book_id); PUT upserts; every write commits; export shows the current rating

subject: list-entries-and-foreign-keys
detail: Readr allows the same book on a list twice and never checks that the list or book exist (SQLite foreign keys are off by default).
solutions: Unique (list_id, book_id), foreign keys on, ownership checks
recommended: Primary key (list_id, book_id), PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, cascade deletes, ownership checked on list and book
